title: Nager.Date public holidays API (Italy, national holidays, v3)
summary: Public REST endpoint returning national public-holiday dates for a given year and ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code. Probed for IT: years 2023, 2024 and 2026 returned HTTP 200 with 13, 13 and 14 holiday records respectively, one record per date with a name in Italian (localName) and English (name). Grain is one row per holiday date, national scope only (global = true, counties = null), which suits labelling sales days for N4. It does not cover regional or patron-saint days, and it has no shop-calendar or event information.

fields.name: fixed
fields.description: Whether the date is fixed each year

fields.name: counties
fields.description: Sub-national region codes when not global; null in sample

fields.name: launchYear
fields.description: Year the holiday was introduced; null in sample

schema.notes: Field list taken from the sample response shape only; no schema document was read. Field types are inferred from the JSON sample.

spatial.notes: Country is passed as ISO alpha-2 in the URL path (e.g. /api/v3/PublicHolidays/2024/IT). Sub-national (regional/patron-saint) holidays are not returned for IT in the probed responses (global = true for all sampled records).

ownership.owner: Nager.Date open-source project (GitHub organisation 'nager', repository nager/Nager.Date)

licence.evidence: Register entry api.nager_public_holidays lists terms_url https://github.com/nager/Nager.Date and agreement_status 'not_required_open_data'. The GitHub repository page (probe_url, fetched 2026-10) shows 'MIT license' for the repository, which is a software licence. No licence statement specific to the holiday data or to the REST API output was found on the page read.

access.request_process: Public GET, no key. Endpoint: https://date.nager.at/api/v3/PublicHolidays/{year}/{country}. One call per year. Register approved_purposes: prototyping, production; production use still needs Legal sign-off under policy.open_data_links.

declared_metadata.contains_pii: no (holiday calendar; no personal fields observed)

documentation_excerpts: Register param_notes: "country is ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 (PT, GB, FR, ...)."

GitHub README (probe_url): "Easily access public holidays for 200+ countries via .NET, REST API, Docker, or NuGet"; the self-hosted Docker section gives the example "curl http://localhost/api/v4/Holidays/US/2026", i.e. a v4 API exists alongside the v3 path used here.
quality_notes: Probe 2024/IT: 13 records, min 2024-01-01, max 2024-12-26. Probe 2023/IT: 13 records, min 2023-01-01, max 2023-12-26. Probe 2026/IT: 14 records, min 2026-01-01, max 2026-12-26. The 2025 year was not probed; the 2025 window (history ends 2025-05-31, recent starts 2025-06-01) therefore relies on the same endpoint pattern, not on a probe.
Record counts differ by year (13 in 2023 and 2024, 14 in 2026); the response does not explain this, so it should be checked against the official calendar before the holiday flag is used.

Scope is national only: all sampled records have global = true and counties = null. Regional and patron-saint days (e.g. local feast days in Valdena's town) are not returned and must be sourced elsewhere if they matter.

Sundays: the flag does not say whether a holiday falls on a Sunday; the day-of-week must be derived by the analyst. The candidate's suspicion that Sunday holidays need a shop-calendar check is consistent with the data shape but is not tested here.

API version drift: the GitHub README documents a v4 path (/api/v4/Holidays/...) for the self-hosted container; the v3 path used in the register was live (HTTP 200) on the probes. Whether v3 is deprecated was not established.
Documentation for the hosted API (docs_url https://date.nager.at/Api) was not read, so update frequency, coverage start year and the data source behind the calendar are not established.

provenance.claim: Endpoint returns HTTP 200 JSON for IT in 2023, 2024 and 2026 with ISO dates and national scope; 13, 13 and 14 records.
Register entry: agreement_status not_required_open_data; approved purposes prototyping and production; endpoint template and param notes (ISO alpha-2 country code).
Repository is MIT-licensed software; no data-specific licence statement was found on the page read.
Local/regional holidays are not included; v4 self-hosted API path exists in README.
Open-data policy: production use of external datasets needs Legal sign-off.

unknowns: Licence of the holiday data itself (only the software repo licence MIT was seen); commercial-use status unknown.
Data source and maintainer behind the calendar; how holidays are curated and when they were last updated.
Whether the 2025 calendar is correct (not probed).
Whether v3 is deprecated or will be retired.
Coverage of the hosted API before 2023 and beyond 2026 (not probed or documented in the sources read).
Refresh cadence and metadata last-updated date.
Whether any Italian holiday falls on a Sunday in the history/recent windows (derivable but not checked here).
